record.title: Harden progress reset across devices with a reset epoch
record.description: Reset progress works server-first for one device, but a second device holding higher local progress would show the old level after a merge. The complete fix adds a reset counter on the server and makes both merge paths discard local data when it advances, which needs an approved database change. It has been held since 2026-11-06; version one may accept the residual risk. The owner delegated judgement calls on 2026-11-10 but a database change still needs explicit approval.

record.title: Give accounts made on the account site a Mazer profile
record.description: Accounts made on the account site, which is what the Mazer Create Account button uses, got no Mazer profile row: only the in-Mazer sign-up path fired the trigger. The profile insert therefore failed with a not-null error on every sign-in, the leaderboard showed Choose a username with no way out, and settings never synced. 111 of 129 accounts had no profile and 9 of them had signed in to Mazer. A profile-ensure database function was applied to the live project on 2026-11-11 with the owner's explicit approval (one new function, no existing object changed; tested with the standing test account: it creates a generated Mazer-###### handle, is idempotent, and refuses a wrong user id and anonymous callers; profile rows 18 to 19). Mazer PRs 446 and 447 make the client call it once per bootstrap and on the settings write path instead of the failing insert; a username save ensures the profile first and a failed save shows a plain toast. Merged and deployed at main 8f757c76 (live bundle checked: the ensure call is present, the old direct insert is gone). The 9 affected players recover on their next load. Headless Chromium and mocks only: no real brand-new-account run and nothing checked on a real phone.

record.title: Widen the sign-in window to 15 minutes and name each sign-in failure
record.description: A family member on a Galaxy S21 could not sign in and every callback failure showed the same message. Mazer's pending sign-in record expired after 5 minutes while the account site allows 15. PR 444 adds seven plain failure messages by class (took too long, came back to a different screen, cancelled, connection, session, storage, generic) and PR 445 wires them and widens the pending window from 5 to 15 minutes; the record is claimed exactly once, so a longer window adds no replay surface. The internal failure code is recorded in diagnostics only, and a new pending-expired code splits took too long from came back to a different screen. Merged and deployed at main 8f757c76. Unit tests plus headless Chromium with failures injected into the live scene at 390 and 1280 widths; no real sign-in round trip with a failure and nothing checked on a real phone. The fix is NOT proven against the original report: her root cause is unconfirmed (see MAZER-ACCT-016).

record.title: Make the Create Account result honest
record.description: The account site Create Account form showed the success-styled notice Your account request is complete. You can continue to your account when a session is available. whenever sign-up returned no session (already registered, a weak new login choice, rate limit, network, unknown) and also after a successful sign-up without a Mazer return context. A family member reported a session was not available, which matches it. FawxzzyWeb PR 121 is MERGED (main bcfc556d) with an honest neutral message instead of the false success text, and a real session now continues straight into the account. It is NOT live: the FawxzzyWeb release carrying it is not yet aliased to the live domains. Residual: with auto-confirm on, a successful sign-up returns a session and a duplicate does not, so whether an account already exists can still be inferred by whether the user ends up signed in; closing that means turning auto-confirm off (see MAZER-ACCT-010). Not checked on a device.

record.title: Decide the Create Account non-enumeration trade-off: accepted, auto-confirm kept
record.description: Owner decision recorded 2026-11-12: accept the residual signal and keep auto-confirm. With auto-confirm on, a successful Create Account returns a session and a duplicate does not, so someone could infer whether an account exists from whether they end up signed in. Closing that fully would mean turning auto-confirm off, which adds a confirmation step for every new player; the rest of the form no longer discloses it and the owner judged that cost not worth paying. No code or setting changed: this card is completed as a decision and has no device surface. Writing the accepted residual into the account site docs is not done and has no card yet.

record.title: Add a leaderboard username editor (Edit name): merged and deployed

record.title: Record a failure code on every sign-in boot failure: deployed, device check pending
record.description: PRs #453 and #454 are merged and live at Mazer main 476c4789 (live bundle strings checked, headless Chromium only). record.title: Receipt typed columns now filled by a trigger and backfill; run-quality use still open
record.description: APPLIED in production by the owner approval of the exact files and verified by readback. A before-insert trigger on the completion receipts fills the typed columns (completion time, path length and the rest), and a batched backfill filled 24,437 existing receipts in 13 batches of 2,000. Readback: all 26,308 receipts have a path length and completion time above zero, the trigger is enabled, no long transactions. Old values are saved in a preimage table; rollback files exist, but a rollback would overwrite later real values on those rows. Limits: the values are asserted by the client and outliers exist (one completion time above 42 million ms), so any run-quality gating must validate them; the typed columns are metadata only today. Lesson recorded: SQL hash guards must be computed from the LIVE function body (the repository copy had LF line endings while the live body had CRLF, so a first version of a stale-name script would have aborted on production), and the production SQL runner role cannot drop or disable triggers on the auth users table (owned by the auth admin role), so rollbacks drop the function with CASCADE. Not a device surface; kept in review until run-quality use is decided.

record.title: Sign-in outage handling: never strand the player on a provider error page
record.description: Outage on 2026-11-12, about 20:35 to 21:11 UTC: the account provider was down (its status page listed Database Connection Errors; the project sign-in and data origin answered 503, then gateway errors 521 and 525) and the owner was left on a blank provider 503 page inside the installed app with no way back. The provider recovered about 21:11 UTC. No data was lost and nothing was caused by our changes: the last database change was more than two hours earlier and sign-in by both routes (account address and username) worked after it. Fix, merged AND deployed (PR #466 at bc912691 and PR #467 at c80d8ce9; production Mazer c80d8ce9): Sign in first asks the account service whether it is up (a 4 second probe of its public discovery document, no sign-in details sent, never stored by the browser, success cached 30 seconds, failures never cached). A 5xx, 4xx, timeout, offline state or a gateway page without the cross-origin header keeps Mazer on Welcome and shows the plain failure line Sign-in is unavailable right now. Try again in a few minutes. with diagnostics code oauth-failure:provider_unreachable; a probe refused in both modes (an extension or content-policy block) falls through and navigates as before. Owner decision accepted: a network error where a follow-up still gets an answer is treated as provider down. Live checks: the bundle carries the new strings and a real sign-in by both routes (account address and username) after the deploy succeeded with no errors. Measured: the first Sign in tap costs 100 to 250 ms more (187 to 247 ms without the probe, 293 to 500 ms with it) and 0 ms inside the 30 second cache window (cache unit-tested only). Kept in review: checked in headless Chromium with mocked failure shapes and against the live service only. NOT verified: a real phone or the installed app, a real outage, browser offline mode, an actual extension block, and a slow-but-up provider (the 4 second limit would block it; the first live probe during recovery took 4.5 seconds upstream).

record.title: Welcome warms the account-service check so Sign in is quick: live, device check open
record.description: MAZER-ACCT-036 added a 4 second pre-flight probe before Sign in leaves the app; measured, the first tap costs 100 to 250 ms more and taps inside the 30 second cache window cost nothing. Proposal: run the same probe quietly when Welcome appears so the cache is already warm at the first tap. Needs a change to the Welcome scene (MenuScene, Wave 5C, a hot file), must never show a failure line by itself, and must not turn a slow-but-up service into a blocked Sign in. Merged and deployed on main 62f36472 (production build fawxzzy-mazer-4djzxfozs, previous build fawxzzy-mazer-ldk3ncpod), checked only in headless Chromium and tests, not on a real phone. PR #470: the Welcome screen runs the 4 second provider probe quietly when it appears and reuses the 30 second success cache. A failed warm-up shows nothing; only a Sign in tap shows the failure line. Measured with a mocked 230 ms probe: the first tap cost fell from 100 to 250 ms to 10 to 40 ms. Not measured against a slow-but-up real service on a phone.

record.title: AI runner calibration: per-band thresholds and checker landed, retention not built
record.description: The previous project board tracked an AI runner that a human can configure, plus a corpus of recorded runs used to calibrate run quality. The runner is nearly done and a first corpus packet exists on main. Remaining gap: calibration is unfinished, and any remote retention of runs would need a provider-side step. Merged to main, no player-visible change, so there is nothing to deploy-check. PR #479 (merged as b6676ace) added per-band calibration thresholds and a checker; the three baselines are unchanged, so no drift. Remote run retention is not built and is recommended dropped. Finding: 68 of 75 seed-pack cases over-deliver complexity against their band. Criteria met except retention, which waits on the owner decision to drop it.

record.title: Compose and wire original Mazer music from the music-language brief

record.title: Make player speed constant and 8% slower: merged and deployed
record.description: Owner request 2026-11-12. PR #449 (merged 73f754c2, live at main f8c16c72; live bundle checked: speed formula v2 present, v1 gone). The step speed used to depend on the Move Speed setting plus a level bonus of up to +0.10 and a pace-score bonus of plus or minus 0.05; now only the setting matters (formula v2) and the step rate is multiplied by 0.92. At the default setting the repeat interval is 139 ms (was 128), about 7.2 steps per second (was 7.8). The touch-stick caps scale to 113, 157 and 157 ms. The menu AI walker is separate and unchanged. Deviation: the stick caps were scaled too, which the owner did not explicitly ask for (a one-line revert). Tested headless and by unit tests; how it feels on a phone was not checked.

record.title: Fade wrap corridors out between levels 100 and 140 and price them
record.description: Wrap corridors used to switch off at level 120 and make level 120 about 88 steps longer than level 119. PR #404 fades them out from level 100 to 140 and prices each wrap's saving the way loops are priced, so a wrap cannot make a level easier than its target. The largest smoothed single-level step in levels 100 to 150 dropped from 19.4 times the median step to 2.3 times. It is merged and deployed on 2026-11-10. The numbers are modelled walker difficulty, not player-tested, and no wrap level was checked on a real phone.

record.title: No one-tile dead-end stubs in generated mazes
record.description: Owner request, with a screenshot of a late maze full of one-tile nubs: stop generating single-tile side branches. Mazer PR #464 is merged (951ef3cf) and deployed to production (the build before it was main 0537aa61). Rule: every generated ladder maze (levels 2 and up) has no dead-end branch shorter than 2 cells; a stub is a dead end whose only neighbour is a junction, and the start and goal caps are exempt. One-cell nubs are lengthened by one cell where the wall has room, else walled up, and each edit is kept only if the felt-difficulty number is unchanged; the fringe (levels 199 to 268 before this change) now carves 2 to 3 cell stubs only. The constant MIN_DEAD_END_BRANCH_CELLS is 2; 3 was not validated. Census before: 1.6 to 3.9 stubs per maze in the middle of the ladder and 51 to 57 per maze at level 268 and up, with 49 to 60 of 60 mazes holding at least one; after: 0 on every band and both boards. AI runner solvability 340 of 340 (levels 1 to 999, both boards, ranks E and S). Headless browser counts: phone level 50 4 to 0, level 150 1 to 0, level 300 32 to 0; desktop level 50 8 to 0, level 150 1 to 0, level 300 51 to 0. CONTRACT CHANGE: the fringe capacity falls from 70 to 20 cells, so the strictly rising ladder now ends at level 218 (was 268) and levels 219 and up are the plateau class. Late mazes lose held-out difficulty (dead ends 81-86 to 31 and decision points 34-40 to 11-13 at the plateau) while the felt number is unchanged; hazards (MAZER-HAZ-002) are meant to supply difficulty past 218. Player impact: most ladder layouts change (157 of 197 phone levels 2 to 198 and 166 of 197 desktop; every level 199 to 300); level 1 is unchanged; progress, receipts and the leaderboard are keyed by level number and seed, not layouts. Only the golden ladder fixture was regenerated. Pull request #464 and its commit named this rule MAZER-GEN-004 before that id was found already used by the wrap-fade card; this card is its board entry. Checked only in headless Chromium and tests, not on a real phone; the owner judgement on the shorter rising ladder is open. Owner informal feedback 2026-11-12 evening, NOT a formal device check: "no single tiles so far". The ladder-end judgement and the preview levels 150, 218 and 300 are still unchecked.

record.title: Straighter ladder mazes, ladder to 288: PR #484 merged and live, owner look pending
record.description: Owner request: reduce the pointless snaking in generated mazes. Measured: pointless snaking (a long run of 10 or more cells with 4 or more tight corners) held 31 to 47 percent of the floor on levels 20 to 218 and above; PR #484 cuts it to 3 to 14 percent by lowering the route share of the felt tuner and making carved branches keep their heading. The strictly rising ladder would extend to level 288 (was 218). PR #484 (merge 5cee1ed2, head e2ae8640) is MERGED AND DEPLOYED (production build fawxzzy-mazer-dyhmua9v6, also on fawxzzy-mazer-dq6f32ysl). It lowers the route share of the felt tuner and makes carved branches keep their heading, then a density fill spends the freed cells on short side branches and breaks long empty halls. Measured before merge: pointless snaking fell to 3 to 14 percent of the floor, zero one-tile stubs, the AI runner solved 340 of 340. Known issues stated in the PR: the fill can read as a comb and sparse seeds are possible. Checked in a headless browser and tests only; no formal device check. The owner gave informal feedback, "no lag, no single tiles so far", which is NOT a formal check. Needs owner device feedback on the comb look and sparse seeds. The preview jump list (MAZER-QA-007) and the ladder length (MAZER-PROG-019) follow. Board update 2026-11-13: Merged and deployed; owner informal feedback: no lag and no single tiles so far (not a formal check). Comb look and sparse seeds still need a phone check at levels 50, 150, 218 and 300. PR #484 merged (5cee1ed2). Deployed: production build fawxzzy-mazer-dyhmua9v6. Checked only in headless Chromium, not on a real phone.

record.title: Stabilise load-sensitive tests: PR #489 merged
record.description: Some tests pass alone every time but fail under parallel load: the endpoint tile pixel test at tile 25.44 and device pixel ratio 3, and vitest worker task-update timeouts. Plan: find the load sensitivity and make them deterministic. Update 2026-11-13: MERGED. PR #489 (merge 0f0f7b7d) is test-side only, so there is no deployed behaviour to check; it is on main, which is deployed at 1dc4e9ca. It adds a vitest configuration with a 60 second default timeout, named heavy tests raised, half the logical CPUs as workers (CI keeps one), a setup file that yields after slow tests, an async runtime-eval test, and a trail frame-cost test that asserts the work instead of wall-clock time. Measured on one machine: three runs at once went from 16 to 20 failed tests to 0 failed with exit 0. Not measured on any other machine. The remaining wall-clock asserts did not fail in any run and were left alone (follow-up suggested). No independent review is recorded.

record.title: Cheaper trail while walking: draft PR #461 needs an owner decision, no pixel parity
record.description: DRAFT PR #461 (head 476e5cf2, CI not started, not merged) splits the trail into a cached older part and a rebuilt tail. It cuts walking frame cost about 1.3 to 2 times (headless proxy, not a phone). Pixel parity with a full rebuild is impossible, because the trail colour changes everywhere every tick: on long routes colour, sheen and breath would step every 250 ms to 1 s instead of moving smoothly. This changes how the game looks, so it needs an OWNER decision after a phone check. Options: A ship it as is; B cap the cache epochs at 500 ms; C keep the smooth colour and accept the lag; D staggered per-chunk recolour or an OffscreenCanvas worker (recommended as the follow-up). Blocked on the owner decision; nothing merged. Owner informal feedback 2026-11-12 evening, NOT a formal check: "no more lag I think". Draft PR #461 stays unmerged; recommended to close it, since the lag no longer shows. Status 2026-11-13: draft PR #461 is still open and unmerged; recommended to close it. The owner decision is still needed.

record.title: Extend the ladder to level 268 with side stubs the explorer does not pay for
record.description: The owner saw that the menu maze for level 18000 looks like a level 30 maze. Every level from 198 was the same maze class because the ladder steers on one explorer number and the board is full at level 198. Shrinking the route to raise that number made the other walkers 40 to 57 percent easier, so it was rejected. The new pull request adds exactly one more cell of short side stubs per level (the explorer does not enter stubs of 3 cells or fewer), which keeps the explorer number fixed and strictly orders levels 199 to 268 by cell count. At level 268 against 198 the maze has 38 route junctions instead of 12, 87 dead ends instead of 27 and the random walk takes 3.6 times as many steps. Levels 1 to 198 are byte-identical and levels 268 and above are one class again; the hazard hand-off now starts at 268. This is an open pull request, not merged and not deployed. The numbers are modelled walker difficulty, not player-tested, and the stubs are visible at a glance to a person. Merged and deployed to the live game on 2026-11-10. Checked only in headless Chromium, not on a real phone.

record.title: Mastery tier to level 388: mazes also hard to solve from the goal end
record.description: Final audit of the progression engine on the frozen boards, without hazards. Finding: the ladder number is an explorer walking from the start, but the board is fully visible, so the same explorer walking from the goal pays only 0.3 to 0.6 of it on every level (475 against 759 at level 198 on the phone board). PR #415 adds a mastery tier for levels 269 to 388: route forks also point toward the start, so the goal end is just as deceptive, with no extra floor and the forward number unchanged. The share of such mazes rises by 1/120 per level to all mazes at level 388, each held to at least 740 steps from the goal end (measured 430 to 475 before, about 760 after). Levels 1 to 268 are byte-identical; the plateau and the hazard hand-off move from 268 to 388. Merged (merge 0a69f679) and deployed to production (main a983f2de, Ready). Honest limits: the ceiling is level 388, the ramp is statistical and not ordered for any two seeds; generation costs about 1.5 times the plateau class and about one desktop mastery build in twenty passed the 400 ms target at a 4x CPU throttle; the phone random walk reads 24 percent easier; no human play-test. Checked only in headless Chromium, not on a real phone or an installed app. Past 388 nothing on this board gets harder without hazards (MAZER-HAZ-002) or a bigger board. Superseded in part by MAZER-PROG-015: the tier is removed in the ladder v2 pull request (open for review) and the plateau returns to level 268.

record.title: Test every database change on a scratch Postgres 17, pin the live hash: PR #491 merged
record.description: Process rule from the 2026-11-12 database work: every SQL proposal is tested on a faithful scratch Postgres 17 and reviewed independently before the owner approves it, and any hash guard pins the md5 of the LIVE function body, not the repository copy (the live body had CRLF line endings, the repository blob LF, and a first guard would have aborted on production). Tooling to build: a reusable scratch Postgres harness and a read-only preimage query pack, both documented in the repository docs. Also record that the production SQL runner role cannot drop or disable triggers on the auth users table, so rollbacks use DROP FUNCTION with CASCADE. Update 2026-11-13: MERGED. PR #491 (merge 6b944ca4) adds the SQL change process document (the rule, the proposal checklist, the failure modes), a checklist line in the pull request template and a pointer in the agent instructions, plus a db-scratch script folder (a scratch Postgres 17 harness and a read-only preimage query pack). Docs and scripts only; nothing deployed, nothing applied to any database. Evidence: the harness self-test passed 20 of 20 checks on a real scratch Postgres 17.9 cluster and 20 unit tests pass. Not verified: pack queries 90 to 92 and the volatile path against the live database; the scratch cluster uses the C locale while production reports en_US.UTF-8. No independent review is recorded. Kept in review until a real SQL change goes through the harness.

record.title: Fix image and vector misalignment: whole-pixel placement and camera origin
record.description: Reported: the end star sat off centre and the trail and player glow jumped as they moved. Root cause: Phaser rounds image positions to whole pixels but not vector graphics, plus a half-pixel camera offset on odd-width viewports; the end star was 2 device pixels off centre at 2.625 and 2.75 pixel ratios and the trail and player glow jumped a CSS pixel as they moved. PR #416 (merge a983f2de) places images on whole pixels, sets the camera origin to 0,0 and snaps the bake margins and maze origin to whole pixels. Merged and deployed to production (Ready, live bundle verified to contain the new code). Checked only in headless Chromium at several viewport sizes and pixel ratios, not on a real phone or an installed app.

record.title: Edge diamonds fill on beam contact, drain on release: merged and live, phone check pending
record.description: Owner request 2026-11-13: redesign the diamond lasers and make the beam fill and drain the diamond, timed to contact. Merged and deployed; not checked on a real phone. PR #492 (merge 1dc4e9ca, head 7a006ab7), live on production build fawxzzy-mazer-dq6f32ysl (Guide copy verified in the shipped bundle). Each edge diamond is empty until the beam head touches it, then fills linearly and is full when the beam tail arrives 200 ms later; on the way out it drains the same way, so the colour leaves through the beam end. Beams are comets in the player colour with a ripple on the contact point. Flight timing, the 400 ms laser and the input unlock are unchanged; the outro ring orbit now starts at 600 ms instead of 400. Reduced Motion shows no travelling beam and a 200 ms crossfade of the diamond fill. The Guide Wrap row now mentions the filling diamonds. Evidence: source, unit, pixel and headless Chromium only. Not checked on a real phone: beam look, contact timing and frame rate on a phone are unknown. No independent review recorded. A design note is in the repository UI docs. Follow-ups: MAZER-VIS-031 and MAZER-VIS-032.
